title: Shortcut Guide
author: kenneth
summary: The current report may still describe intended hold-to-open behavior, because it never says which trigger mode is in use and the only follow-up comment explicitly reminds the reporter to keep holding the Windows key.

judgment.rationale: Before proposing code changes, maintainers need one narrow clarification: whether the reporter is using the hold-Windows-key activation path or the regular shortcut path, and whether the overlay disappears while the Windows key is still held.
evidence: The body never says whether Shortcut Guide was opened by holding the Windows key or by the configurable regular shortcut.
The expected behavior claims the guide should stay open until click-away or Esc, which can conflict with the hold-Windows-key close-on-release behavior.
A follow-up commenter says, "You have to keep holding down the Windows key part of the shortcut."
ShortcutGuideActivationPolicy.cs explicitly distinguishes RegularHotkey from WindowsKeyHold and allows close-on-Windows-key-release when the hold path is used.
judgment.recommended_action: Ask for a bounded trigger-mode confirmation before deciding whether this is a real bug or an intended hold-to-open behavior.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current public report may describe expected Windows-key-hold behavior, so proposing a fix before clarifying the trigger mode would be premature.

issue_context.summary: Shortcut Guide disappears too quickly according to the reporter, but the thread still does not distinguish the hold-Windows-key mode from the regular hotkey mode.
known_information: The issue is on PowerToys 0.100.2 and includes a bug-report ZIP.
The reporter says the guide loads but does not stay active long enough to read.
The only follow-up comment says to keep holding the Windows key.
No assignee or linked fix exists.
inferences: The issue may be a misunderstanding of the Windows-key-hold activation semantics rather than a fresh regression.
If the overlay also disappears while the Windows key remains held, then it becomes a real bug rather than expected close-on-release behavior.
issue_context.analysis: A precise behavior-confirmation request is the right next step. The dashboard should not expose a fix design until the trigger mode is clarified.
initial_investigation: ShortcutGuideActivationPolicy.GetActivationAction() and ShouldCloseOnWindowsKeyRelease() show different behavior for RegularHotkey versus WindowsKeyHold.
The issue body does not mention changing Close on Windows key release or using the configurable regular shortcut.

information_gaps.information: Whether the reporter opens Shortcut Guide by holding the Windows key or by the configurable regular shortcut.
information_gaps.why_needed: This determines whether the current behavior might simply match the intended hold-to-open path.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reply with the exact Shortcut Guide activation method currently configured and how you are triggering it when the issue occurs.

information_gaps.information: Whether the overlay disappears while the Windows key is still held, or only after the Windows key is released.
information_gaps.why_needed: This separates an expected close-on-release flow from a real premature-dismissal bug.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Reproduce once and describe whether the guide vanishes before or after you release the Windows key.

actions.label: Confirm trigger mode and close-on-release behavior

comment.body:
Thanks for the report. Before we propose code changes, we need to separate a real dismissal bug from the built-in “hold Windows key” behavior that can close Shortcut Guide when the key is released.

**Needed**
1. Please confirm whether you are opening Shortcut Guide by holding the Windows key or by using the configurable regular shortcut.
2. Please confirm whether the guide disappears while the Windows key is still held down, or only after you release it.

Those two details will tell us whether this is an actual premature-dismissal bug or the expected close-on-release path for the hold-to-open mode.
